title: Standby synchronizer and fallback variant conductor
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Background: We currently rely on simple region-priority routing with ad-hoc warm standby priming. During recent rehearsals we observed inconsistent KV cache freshness across standby fleets, slow traffic ramp when activating a standby region, and suboptimal fallback selection when a primary model variant is unavailable. This ticket implements a coordinated "standby synchronizer" component that (1) performs state reconciliation (model binary, KV cache checkpoints, quantization profile tags), (2) runs multi-tier preflight probes with an aggregate readiness score, and (3) drives the "fallback variant conductor" which maps failed variants to compatible degraded variants and orchestrates progressive traffic shift.

Goals: Reduce failover convergence time to <30s for typical region switchovers, ensure >95% of production request prefixes hit warm cache after cutover, provide clear telemetry for readiness scoring and reduce customer error-rate on failover from observed 7% -> <1%.

Scope: Implement control-plane orchestrator (service) + agent hooks in serving runtime for priming and verification. Integrations: routing service (smart-router), console rollouts UI, telemetry pipelines (datadog -> observability dashboards), and an API for explicit rehearsals.

Design summary:
- Standby synchronizer: central coordinator that tracks intended model version and expected cache checkpoints for each standby pool. Uses quorum of probes across N machines to compute "cache-warmth" and "model-ready" bits.
- Preflight probe types: binary-serving-check, kv-prefix-scan latency, sample-inference-smoke (latency + output-hash), token-consumption-sample (verify quantization/ops path), and disk-health.
- Readiness score: weighted aggregate (model-ready 40%, kv-warmth 30%, smoke-infer 20%, infra-health 10%). Thresholds: green >= 0.85, amber 0.6-0.85, red <0.6.
- Fallback variant conductor: declarative policy repository mapping primary->degraded candidates (e.g., 8-bit quantized variant, shorter context variant, smaller model family). Conductor performs compatibility checks (vocab/tokenizer, max-seq), runs a smoke-mix test, and if compatible, stages traffic via routing policies with progressive percentages and automated rollback on regressed quality metrics.

Non-goals: full autoscaler changes, long-lived cross-region KV streaming (we will rely on checkpoint copying and targeted prefetching).

High-level rollout plan:
1) Implement synchronizer service + probe framework (internal API) behind feature flag.
2) Add agent probe hooks to serving runtime and implement lightweight checkpoint validation endpoints.
3) Wire conductor to smart-router to apply progressive policy changes (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and expose rehearsal endpoints in Console.
4) Run staged rehearsals in staging, then canary in low-traffic customer pool, full rollout if metrics meet thresholds.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- Failover convergence time (target <30s). Metric: time from routing change to >90% traffic served by target region.
- Prefix cache hit rate after cutover (target >95% within 60s).
- Smoke-infer success rate (target >99%).
- Automated anomaly detection: if fallback increases mean-latency >20% or error-rate >1% absolute, trigger rollback.

Security/Compliance: Synchronizer will access model artifacts and KV cache metadata. KMS keys are required for artifact signatures; security_review_required is set and we will add an allowlist for endpoints.

Runtime probes implemented and return stable smoke-infer hashes across 95% of nodes in staging
Readiness score computed and emitted to telemetry; green/amber/red thresholds visible in Console
Fallback conductor can apply a staged routing policy and rollback automatically when quality gates fail
